proposals.title: Dashboard views counter: pull back from a stat card on a phone as the number races up
proposals.why: DJ3 whole: one CAM CTRL null scales the scene 195.8% to 100% while the frame racks into focus (blur 40 to 0 in 0.3 s) and a green trend arrow + counter run 6.8M to 42.8M with a trailing label, over a blurred app screen and phone edge.
proposals.call: viewsCounterCard(comp, {at, title: "Professional dashboard", label: "views in the last 30 days", from: 6.8, to: 42.8, decimals: 1, suffix: "M", countDuration: 1.9333, color: "#5ceb45", zoomFrom: 195.81, focusBlur: 40})
proposals.overlaps: uses countUp, trendArrow, statCard, nullPullBack, defocusIn, focusFalloffUI, phoneEdgeCloseup, sideFalloff; nothing in the kit yet

proposals.title: Fast pull-back on a parent null that glides into a slow creep
proposals.why: Every layer is parented to CAM CTRL; its scale goes 195.81% to 104.074% in 2.17 s (out -425%/s at 1.97% influence, in 95.12%) then creeps to 100% by 4.23 s, speeding up slightly so the shot still moves at the cut.
proposals.call: nullPullBack(comp, {at, from: 195.81, settle: 104.074, end: 100, duration: 2.1667, creep: 2.0667})
proposals.overlaps: cameraDrift (proposals.json) is the slow push; this is the launch-and-glide pull-back that hands off into a drift. Could be a `pullBack` option of cameraDrift.

proposals.title: Rack into focus: whole-frame blur 40 to 0 in 0.3 s
proposals.why: An adjustment layer with Gaussian Blur (Repeat Edge Pixels) drops from 40 to 0 over 0.3 s, still moving when it lands, so the scene clicks sharp as the shot starts.

proposals.title: Number that counts up from a keyed slider
proposals.why: Counter's Source Text reads CAM CTRL's Views (M) slider with .toFixed(1) + "M"; the slider launches at 220/s (1% influence) and glides in (95%), so most of the count happens in the first 0.4 s.
proposals.call: countUp(textLayer, {from: 6.8, to: 42.8, at, duration: 1.9333, decimals: 1, suffix: "M"})

proposals.title: Label that stays a fixed gap right of a changing text
proposals.why: Views Label's x is Counter's right edge (sourceRectAtTime) + 15 px every frame, so the words slide over as the number gets wider.

proposals.title: Glowing green trend arrow (up-right) before a number
proposals.why: A 43 px stroked arrow (#5ceb45, 6.5 px, round caps/joins) with Deep Glow (radius 150, exposure 0.02) and a shimmering CC Light Sweep: the 'growth' cue next to the stat.

proposals.title: Light sweep across an accent
proposals.why: CC Light Sweep (Smooth, width 50, sweep 50, edge 100, white, Add) on the arrow; here the direction is wiggle(1,100), a continuous shimmer (DJ4 uses a keyed one-shot pass).
proposals.overlaps: same as lightSweep in proposals.json; key the angle instead of wiggle so rebuilds match

proposals.title: Deep Glow on accent shapes and numbers
proposals.why: Deep Glow radius 150, exposure 0.02, spread 33 makes the green arrow bloom on the dark card.

proposals.title: Dark dashboard stat card: soft title, sharp number, soft label
proposals.why: 1512x345 r24 card with a 5-stop vertical gradient (#15171b to #272b30 to #202428), grey title (SF Pro Medium 86, #454950, blur 2.5), white number (Regular 69) and grey label (#42454d, blur 1.5): focus lands on the number.
proposals.call: statCard(comp, {title, value, label, x, y, width})
proposals.overlaps: none; would host countUp + trendArrow + trailingLabel

proposals.title: Blurred skeleton app screen behind the focal element (shallow focus)
proposals.why: Placeholder header bars + story-highlight circles drawn as shapes and blurred more the further they are from the number (1.5, 2.5, 3, 9, 12): a flat comp that reads as a macro shot of a real app.

proposals.title: Macro of a phone's side edge: button, metallic rail, bezel
proposals.why: Four gradient rects (side button, 9-stop metallic rail, bezel edge, dark screen) blurred 3 give the bright sliver of hardware that sells 'this is on a phone'.
proposals.overlaps: phoneMock (proposals.json) is a whole phone; this is the extreme close-up

proposals.title: One-side light falloff (multiply ramp)
proposals.why: A Multiply solid with a linear ramp white at x 1200 to 15% grey at x 1950 shades the right of the frame so the card fades into darkness.
proposals.overlaps: background (that is the backdrop; this is a shading pass on top)
